title: Corey Blues Lesson
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Granddaddy spun it slow
From a porch with worn-out paint
Bottle on the rail
And a voice that never fainted
He said the hard times sing
If you let 'em have a name
And every scar got teeth
When the night began to rain

[Pre-Chorus]
I leaned in close
Like I was six years old
He said, son, don't chase the shine
Chase the hurt that made 'em bold

[Chorus]
History of blues
Sang to me, Corey
History of blues
Right there in the morning
Keep it low
Keep it true
History of blues
Sang to me, Corey

[Verse 2]
Mama had a church fan
Papa had a factory cough
A penny in the jar
And a bill they couldn't cross
Railroad towns and river mud
Boot soles caked in black
Every road I ever knew
Had a broken heart in back

[Pre-Chorus]
I heard it in the fields
I heard it in the train
Heard it in the kitchen
When nobody said his name

[Chorus]
History of blues
Sang to me, Corey
History of blues
Right there in the morning
Keep it low
Keep it true
History of blues
Sang to me, Corey

[Bridge]
Now I carry that old tune
In the pocket of my coat
Not a chain, not a wound
Just a fire, just a note
If you ask me where I learned
How to hold a little pain
I point back to that porch
And I say it once again

[Chorus]
History of blues
Sang to me, Corey
History of blues
Right there in the morning
Keep it low
Keep it true
History of blues
Sang to me, Corey
